translation_direction: ja → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Japanese electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: The ironic, learned narrator, Nami’s quickness and the rustic village voices are kept in elegant, crisp Vietnamese with the essayistic digressions lucid and the poems translated for sense.
decisions.rationale: The narrator’s pose and its failure are the book’s subject.

decisions.decision: The Japanese text comes from Aozora Bunko, with ruby readings removed and the embedded JIS X 0213 characters restored; it is translated directly from the Japanese, not from an English version.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: ‘住みにくい’, the refrain of the famous opening, was rendered ‘khó ở’ (unwell); now ‘khó sống’, and the first paragraph is four balanced clauses with the refrain.
The sentence on probing motives had the ordinary novelist as its subject, losing the narrator’s own risk of vulgarity; restored.
‘ぴしゃりと焼き付いた’ was rendered unintelligibly; corrected.
‘山姥’ (a mountain hag) was rendered as a mountain maiden; now ‘mụ sơn quỷ’.
The clause ‘花を厭えば足を着くるに地なき’ was garbled; rewritten.
A kanshi line was transliterated; it is now translated for sense, as the house rule requires (‘Bóng trúc quét thềm, bụi chẳng động’).
The corner of the building and the tall woman swapped roles; corrected after the last blind review, by hand.
The Inari-fox rank and the young-lord allusions of a haiku were lost; now ‘Hồ ly Chính nhất vị’ and ‘Công tử’ with the sense carried.
‘言語道断’ was rendered as a meaningless calque; now ‘quả là quá quắt, không nói nên lời’.
The Kanjincho lyric was rendered as an assertion about Okura, then its last clause made the singer recognise her own song; fixed twice, the second time by hand after the last blind review.
‘十分の美’ (full beauty) was rendered as one tenth of beauty; corrected.
The paired ‘ためか…ためか’ questions about the Venice couple were merged into one garbled sentence; restored.
‘洒落’ (breezy, unfettered) was rendered ‘ngạo nghễ’ (arrogant) three times; now ‘phóng khoáng/tiêu sái’.
The concession (the faces are visible, yet the bond is already cut) was turned into a conditional; now ‘Dù… dù… dù…’.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.rationale: The refrain of the opening; ‘khó ở’ means unwell.
The narrator’s aesthetic detachment, kept as Sino-Vietnamese without gloss.
The Zen monk’s unfettered manner, not arrogance.
No kanshi or haiku is left transliterated.

witness_decision: Selected the Aozora Bunko electronic text of Natsume Soseki’s 草枕 (card 776), which cites Chikuma Bunko’s Natsume Soseki Zenshu 3 (Chikuma Shobo, 1987) and, for that, the Chikuma Zenshu Ruijuban (1971–72) as its source, with first publication in Shinshosetsu, September 1906; the project did not collate it with a printed edition.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The haiku in unit 1052 lacks the house ‘ / ’ line breaks.
The mat stops just short of the water in the Japanese; the Vietnamese lets the toes touch it.
Nami’s ‘go and die’ is softer than the cruelly direct Japanese.
‘憐れ’ is rendered ‘thương xót’, leaning toward pity rather than tender sorrow.

title_review.rationale: The title is rendered as ‘Gối cỏ’ (grass pillow); no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: ‘Climbing a mountain path, I thought: if you work with your intellect, you grow sharp-cornered…’.
The last unit: the painter’s picture is completed in an instant by Nami’s look of pity.
